_comment: Capabilities this repository's documents (or its own API contracts) CLAIM,
that the code does not do as claimed. The shape is gnomon's
conformance/declared_not_implemented.json, widened from enumeration values to
capabilities, because this repository's gap is wider: the Sep 2026 audit found
docs marking a finished Phase 1 over heuristics, a constant confidence
interval and an LLM layer nothing calls.
Every entry carries:
claimed_in  where the claim is made, as {at: 'file:line', says: <quote>}.
'file@rev:line' cites a committed revision (the claim was
published there and has since been withdrawn from the tree).
reality     one line: what the code actually does.
evidence    code locations that make `reality` true, same {at, says} shape.
leaves_by   what must exist for the entry to leave the list: a test (path +
what it asserts), a CI run, or a retraction of the claim.
status      declared-not-implemented | partial | planned -- the same token
docs/CURRENT_STAGE.md shows for it.
scripts/status_claims.py checks every citation: the quote must still be in
the cited file (on the cited line, or it reports the drift). A quote that is
GONE fails the gate, because then this register says something about the code
or the docs that is no longer true -- which is the defect it exists to catch.
An entry leaves this list by being IMPLEMENTED (its leaves_by exists and
passes) or by the claim being RETRACTED from the docs -- never by being
dropped. When one leaves, it moves to `left_the_list` with the commit and the
test that pins it.

declared_not_implemented.capability: Counterfactual reasoning over a structural causal model

claimed_in.says: Structural causal model (SCM), observation, query (intervention or counterfactual)

declared_not_implemented.reality: No structural causal model is fitted anywhere. counterfactual_reason is now a labelled heuristic that reports identification_status NOT_ASSESSED and makes no quantitative claim (it previously reported IDENTIFIED from edge confidences and invented impact-reduction percentages). causal-core refuses rung-3 queries with RUNG_MISMATCH.

leaves_by.asserts: for a known SCM and observed unit, the counterfactual outcome under do(T=t') equals the analytic value (and equals the factual outcome when t' is the factual treatment)

declared_not_implemented.capability: Causal discovery: candidate edges and independence tests from data

claimed_in.says: Proposes candidate edges, confounders, mediators, and missing variables in the causal graph from data and document evidence.

declared_not_implemented.reality: The discovery agent proposes one edge between two freshly generated uuid4() nodes with a confidence looked up from the Cynefin domain; conditional_independence_test is a stub that returns None.

leaves_by.asserts: on data simulated from a known DAG the recovered skeleton/CPDAG is within a pre-registered structural Hamming distance of the truth

declared_not_implemented.capability: Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding (E-values, Rosenbaum bounds)

claimed_in.says: Computes Rosenbaum sensitivity bounds and E-values for unmeasured confounders

declared_not_implemented.reality: E-values are now correct and scale-aware (causal-core's e_value_rr; risk ratio, or difference plus outcome SD; otherwise null with the reason), and the kernel reports E-values and Cinelli-Hazlett robustness values from data. Rosenbaum bounds are not implemented: rosenbaum_gamma is always null (the previous values came from an invented multiplier).

leaves_by.asserts: Rosenbaum bounds match a published matched-pairs example (E-values are already pinned by backend/tests/unit/test_effect_estimate.py)

declared_not_implemented.capability: EconML / PyMC estimation backends
declared_not_implemented.reality: Neither EconML nor PyMC is a dependency; estimation is causal-core (and DoWhy is no longer a backend dependency either). causal-core's plug-in registry is the way to add EconML estimators.

leaves_by.asserts: the claims are removed from the docs -- or the dependency is added with a test that exercises an estimator from it

declared_not_implemented.capability: Rust crates (cynepic-causal, cynepic-bayes) backing DAG operations and belief tracking
declared_not_implemented.reality: This repository contains no Rust code and depends on no crate; the cynepic crates belong to separate projects that were inspiration only.

leaves_by.asserts: the crate references are removed from the docs and the docstrings that repeat them

declared_not_implemented.capability: Capability-based LLM routing used by the agents

claimed_in.says: the LLM factory resolves capability → provider at runtime

declared_not_implemented.reality: get_llm has no call site outside its own docstring: no agent invokes an LLM, and every agent's reasoning is rule or heuristic code.

leaves_by.asserts: an agent path requests a capability through get_llm and its output depends on the (stubbed) model's reply

declared_not_implemented.capability: Guardian verdicts that authorise exactly one write: bound to the object, single-use, unforgeable

claimed_in.says: Guardian verdict IDs are validated against the audit log before writes proceed
All verdicts are immutable once written

declared_not_implemented.reality: The registry checks only that the verdict id exists in audit_log with verdict APPROVED: not that it was issued for this object or payload, not that it is unused, and it carries no signature -- one APPROVED row authorises any number of unrelated writes (replay), and anything that can insert into audit_log can mint one (forge).

leaves_by.asserts: a verdict issued for object A is refused for object B; a verdict is refused on second use; an audit_log row inserted without the issuer's key is refused

declared_not_implemented.capability: API approval flow: POST /api/governance/check then POST /api/governance/approve

claimed_in.says: The caller must supply a valid Guardian verdict_id (from a previous
Guardian approval workflow (DRAFT → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED → DEPRECATED)

declared_not_implemented.reality: /check builds its EpistemicState with no Cynefin domain, which defaults to DISORDER, and Guardian rule PR-006 rejects every verdict in DISORDER -- so /check never returns APPROVED and /approve can never be satisfied through the API.

leaves_by.asserts: a compliant payload in a classified domain gets APPROVED from /check, and /approve with that verdict_id promotes the object

declared_not_implemented.capability: Approval notes and rejection reasons recorded in the audit trail

claimed_in.says: notes: str | None = Field(None, description="Optional approval notes")
formally approve a proposed intervention with a reason attached, so the decision is recorded in the audit trail

declared_not_implemented.reality: approve_object never passes the notes on, so they are discarded; a rejection's reason reaches audit_log only inside the SHA-256 payload_hash. No reason text is stored anywhere.

leaves_by.asserts: approve notes and reject reason are returned as text by GET /api/governance/audit-log for the decision's entry

declared_not_implemented.capability: Reject validates the Guardian verdict it is given

claimed_in.says: description="ID of the Guardian REJECTED audit_log entry"

declared_not_implemented.reality: RejectRequest requires verdict_id, but reject_object never reads it: any UUID is accepted.

leaves_by.asserts: /reject with an unknown or non-REJECTED verdict_id is refused with a 4xx

declared_not_implemented.capability: Review queue ordered by risk tier, showing who submitted each item

claimed_in.says: summary="List pending drafts ordered by risk tier"

declared_not_implemented.reality: ReviewQueueItem carries no risk tier and no submitter, the queue is not ordered by risk, and the UI fills riskTier "MEDIUM" and submittedBy "system" for every item.

leaves_by.asserts: /review-queue returns risk_tier and submitted_by derived from each object and orders by risk tier

declared_not_implemented.capability: Audit-log requests bounded by the client's `limit`

claimed_in.says: auditLog: (params?: { from?: string; to?: string; limit?: number })

declared_not_implemented.reality: GET /api/governance/audit-log reads page and page_size; the client's `limit` query parameter is silently ignored and page_size defaults to 100.

leaves_by.asserts: the number of rows returned honours the limit the client sends (either the endpoint accepts `limit` or the client sends `page_size`)

declared_not_implemented.capability: Provenance records written by real platform flows
declared_not_implemented.reality: store_provenance_record has no call site: nothing outside the tests writes a provenance record, so the provenance API serves only what tests put there.

leaves_by.asserts: a real flow (e.g. POST /api/v1/session/run) produces a provenance record retrievable from the provenance API

declared_not_implemented.capability: TLA+ model of Guardian policy, model-checked in CI

claimed_in.says: verified in CI via TLC model checker
Critical safety properties verified by this spec

declared_not_implemented.reality: No CI job runs TLC, and the spec cannot be checked as written: it uses Range, which none of its EXTENDS'd standard modules define, and Next quantifies over STRING, which TLC cannot enumerate.

leaves_by.asserts: a CI step runs TLC on specs/guardian_policy.tla with guardian_policy.cfg to completion with no violation, and a deliberately broken copy is rejected

declared_not_implemented.capability: Neo4j as the causal graph store (d-separation and backdoor-path queries)
declared_not_implemented.reality: The semantic layer (fragments, edges) is stored through SQLAlchemy (SQLite/PostgreSQL); Neo4j code exists only for the experience buffer and drift alerts, is exercised only against mocks, and no d-separation or path query runs in Neo4j.

leaves_by.asserts: against a real Neo4j (the docker-compose service), the paths that claim Neo4j store and query what they claim to

declared_not_implemented.capability: Kafka event streaming (ingestion bus, alert emission)

claimed_in.says: Alert emission via Kafka ready for integration
The platform requires PostgreSQL 16, Neo4j 5, Kafka (KRaft), and Redis.

declared_not_implemented.reality: No Kafka client is a dependency or imported anywhere; the connector base class carries a comment to replace its stub with a producer. docker-compose starts a broker nothing talks to.

leaves_by.asserts: an alert produced by the platform is consumed from the broker

declared_not_implemented.capability: Unified graph-authoring UI (DAG Workbench)
declared_not_implemented.reality: Not built. The frontend has per-page components; no unified authoring surface exists.

leaves_by.asserts: a user can propose a fragment, see Guardian's verdict, and submit it for approval from one surface

declared_not_implemented.capability: Triangulation flags outcome-model misspecification in causal-core

claimed_in.says: Estimators that rest on different assumptions are compared

declared_not_implemented.reality: Measured power against a planted misspecification that biases regression adjustment by ~0.16 (~1.2 SE of the difference): 0.035 at n=2,000 (reported), 1.00 at n=50,000 (gated). At moderate n, 'estimators agree' is weak evidence that a model is right.

leaves_by.asserts: a pre-registered triangulation power >= 0.80 at n <= 5,000 against a planted misspecification, e.g. via an added specification test or flexible-learner arm

declared_not_implemented.capability: Estimation of effects identified only by the general ID algorithm (e.g. the napkin graph)
declared_not_implemented.reality: causal-core identifies such effects and returns the ID expression, then refuses with NO_ESTIMATOR: no estimator for arbitrary ID functionals exists.

leaves_by.asserts: a napkin-graph estimation case in T0 with bias <= 3 MCSE and pre-registered coverage

declared_not_implemented.capability: causal-core methods beyond the current portfolio: nonparametric front-door, discovery, time series, anytime-valid sequential tests, interference-aware designs
declared_not_implemented.reality: Listed as not implemented in the package README; none of these exists in the kernel.

leaves_by.asserts: each method leaves this entry separately, with its own pre-registered T0 case and seeded defect

declared_not_implemented.capability: Positivity violations detected before estimation
declared_not_implemented.reality: The check reads a logistic propensity model. IHDP's by-construction overlap violation (all treated children of non-white mothers removed) was not detected from its 25 covariates in 100/100 realizations; the ATE was answered by extrapolation (coverage stayed >= 0.97).

evidence.says: a refusal needs a detectable overlap violation

leaves_by.asserts: a pre-registered IHDP bar that the ATE is refused or flagged for the overlap violation, e.g. via a flexible or covariate-profile overlap check

the governance UI showed approvals and audit rows that no backend call had confirmed
planned: packages/causal-core -- identification before estimation, influence-function intervals, typed refusals, a claim contract and a pre-registered T0 correctness gate
left_the_list.note: The backend skills and the backend MCP server do not use it (packages/causal-mcp, a separate server, does), so the platform rows (intervals, identification, frontdoor, sensitivity) stay open until the backend does.

left_the_list.was: partial: ATE point estimation (backdoor linear regression, IV) via DoWhy
left_the_list.fixed_in: the backend rewire onto causal-core (git log -- backend/src/skills/_kernel.py)
left_the_list.note: Backend effect estimates now come from causal-core: identification from the fragment graph, design checks, IF-based intervals. Ground-truth bias and coverage are pinned by the kernel's T0 gate; the backend test pins that the skill returns the kernel's estimate and interval on simulated confounded data.

left_the_list.was: declared-not-implemented: Confidence intervals on effect estimates
left_the_list.fixed_in: the backend rewire onto causal-core (git log -- backend/src/skills/_kernel.py)
left_the_list.note: No code path in backend/src returns a constant interval (scanned by test_no_code_path_returns_a_constant_interval). Intervals are causal-core's; their coverage is gated by T0 (pooled 94.9%) and the real-data benchmarks.

left_the_list.fixed_in: the backend rewire onto causal-core (git log -- backend/src/skills/_kernel.py)
left_the_list.note: Strategy labels now come from causal-core's identification certificate, so a front-door label means front-door. Linear front-door estimation is gated by T0 (frontdoor_continuous). Reachable from the backend when a fragment node has no data column (it becomes latent).

left_the_list.was: declared-not-implemented: Causal identification (is the effect identifiable, by which strategy, with which adjustment set)
left_the_list.fixed_in: the backend rewire onto causal-core (git log -- backend/src/skills/_kernel.py)
left_the_list.note: identification_check runs causal-core's identification (complete ID algorithm plus back-door/front-door/IV) on the fragment graph. The literature catalog and the y0 cross-check are gated by T0.

The four runs before it failed on an unpinned mcp range, unpinned lint tools, a frontend typecheck reading a stale dist/, a coverage floor measured with a gitignored .env present, and FastAPI 0.141's lazy routers.
